Why this chain

Built so one person can run Sunday.

The choice that shapes this setup is one operator. Two PTZ cameras on presets mean nobody stands behind a tripod: the wide camera never moves, and the second one recalls “pulpit”, “worship” and “announcements” at the press of a button.

The switcher is the ATEM Mini Pro because it has a button per input and streams on its own, with no computer in the signal path. Its four HDMI inputs take the two cameras, the slides computer and one spare. When the church wants Monday’s edit to re-cut the sermon from each camera, the ATEM Mini Pro ISO is the drop-in swap.

Sound goes through a 12-channel mixer that records each channel, because a stream mix is hard to get right live. Last week’s tracks also let the sound volunteer rehearse without the band.

Small church setup questions.

Cost, crew, what is missing and tax.

What does a small church livestream setup cost?

This one adds up to $7,416.99 at listed prices for 6 items and 8 pieces, before sales tax and shipping. Untick what you already own and the total follows.

Can one volunteer run it?

Yes. The two cameras sit on presets, the switcher has a button per camera, and the operator wears headphones to hear what the stream hears.

What is not included?

Cables, camera mounts, a computer for slides, and your internet connection. Long camera runs need SDI cable and a converter at the switcher; a specialist adds these for your room.

Does this setup need NDI or a network switch?

No. The cameras connect by video cable (HDMI, or SDI with a converter) and the switcher streams over the church’s Ethernet. The larger three-PTZ setup uses the network for cameras.

Can we buy it tax-free?

Religious institutions with an approved exemption certificate pay no sales tax. Attach the certificate at checkout or send it with the quote.
